patient_actor_hidden.Past_Medical_History: History of being a professional athlete. No significant past medical history reported.
patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: Retired, does not smoke or drink alcohol excessively.

objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and diagnose the patient presenting with long-term bilateral wrist and knee pain.

turns.doctor_opening: Hello, what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what's been going on?
turns.patient_opening: Doctor: Hello—what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what’s been going on? Patient: I’m a 55-year-old retired professional athlete, and over the last 10 years I’ve had pain in both my wrists and knees. In the mornings I get stiffness that lasts about 50 minutes, but I don’t notice swelling, color changes in my fingers, dry mouth/eyes, or any fever or chills.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any swelling in your joints?
turns.patient_answer: Patient: No, I haven’t noticed any swelling in my wrists or knees, and I don’t have any color changes in my fingers either.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any bumps, sores, or unusual spots on your scalp?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any bumps, sores, or unusual spots on my scalp. I’ve mostly just had the ongoing wrist and knee pain and that morning stiffness for about 50 minutes.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been experiencing any itching or a feeling of itchiness anywhere on your body?
turns.patient_answer: Patient: No, I haven’t noticed any itching or a feeling of itchiness anywhere on my body.

turns.doctor_question: Do you have any trouble raising your arms above your head?
turns.patient_answer: Patient: Not really—I can raise my arms over my head without much trouble, though the wrists and knees can ache more afterward.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any loss of vision that isn’t accompanied by pain?
turns.patient_answer: Patient: No, I haven’t noticed any vision loss or anything like that. It’s mainly been the ongoing wrist and knee pain with morning stiffness that lasts around 50 minutes.

turns.doctor_question: Have you had a fever that’s felt extremely hot—like a temperature above 104 °F (40 °C) that’s made you feel dizzy or very uncomfortable?
turns.patient_answer: No, I haven’t had any fever that high, and I haven’t felt dizzy or extremely unwell from feeling feverish. The main issue has been the long-standing pain in my wrists and knees with about 50 minutes of morning stiffness.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling unusually stressed or overwhelmed lately?
turns.patient_answer: Patient: No, I wouldn’t say I’ve been unusually stressed or overwhelmed lately. My main issue has been the long-standing pain in my wrists and knees and the morning stiffness that lasts about 50 minutes.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any burning or discomfort when you urinate?
turns.patient_answer: Patient: No, I haven’t noticed any burning or discomfort when I urinate. It’s mainly the ongoing wrist and knee pain with morning stiffness lasting about 50 minutes.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling chills lately?
turns.patient_answer: Patient: No, I haven’t been feeling chills—no fever or chills at all. It’s mainly the long-standing pain in both my wrists and knees with morning stiffness that lasts about 50 minutes.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any firm lumps in your breast that feel fixed and don’t move when you touch them?
turns.patient_answer: No, I haven’t noticed any firm lumps in my chest or breasts—nothing fixed or unmoving that I can feel.

turns.doctor_question: Are you feeling any pain on the sides of your abdomen or back, near your kidneys?
turns.patient_answer: Patient: No, I haven’t had pain on the sides of my abdomen or back near my kidneys. It’s mainly been the ongoing wrist and knee pain with morning stiffness that lasts about 50 minutes.

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel pain in your calf when you walk, and does it go away when you stop and rest?
turns.patient_answer: Patient: No, I don’t have calf pain when I walk that forces me to stop and rest—the main discomfort is in my wrists and knees, especially with the morning stiffness that lasts about 50 minutes.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed that your urine looks darker than usual?
turns.patient_answer: Patient: No, I haven’t noticed my urine looking darker than usual. It’s mostly just the long-standing pain in my wrists and knees with morning stiffness that lasts around 50 minutes.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any difficulty moving your arm up or across your body?
turns.patient_answer: Patient: No, I haven’t had any real difficulty moving my arms up or across my body—mostly it’s just the wrist and knee aches, and the morning stiffness that lasts about 50 minutes.

turns.doctor_question: Do you notice joint pain or stiffness after doing the same repetitive motion—like typing, lifting, or other repetitive tasks—for a while?
turns.patient_answer: Patient: Not specifically—my wrists and knees mainly hurt and stiffen in the mornings, and the pain tends to linger a bit with activity afterward rather than clearly flaring just from one repetitive motion.
